sections.title: From conflict back to peace
sections.content: *kibékül valakivel* ("to make up with someone") is the natural next step after *összevész* — and like it, the other person takes *-val/-vel*, never an accusative object. Put *egymással* after it and you get the reciprocal *kibékülnek egymással*, "they make up with each other." *megbocsát* works differently: the person you forgive is dative (*megbocsátok neked*), while the thing you forgive is accusative (*megbocsátom a hibát*) — you can use either alone or both together.

sections.title: Reconciliation
rows: we make up with each other

items.english: We fell out, but then we made up.

sections.content: *megbocsát* is definite-conjugated only when there is a stated accusative object: *megbocsátom a hibát* (definite, because *a hibát* is a specific object) but *megbocsátok neked* (indefinite, because *neked* is dative — it isn't an accusative object at all). Don't force a definite ending just because the sentence is about forgiving a specific person.
